question.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability on an Unbounded Interval
question.worked_solution:
If $Z∼N(0,1),$ then by the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

Also, since $Z$ is continuous, 

$$
P(Z<2.01)=P(Z\le 2.01)=Φ(2.01).
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069404/assets/300726cc3cff6cb943d627693bdea3da57ca7bb814988b55e9e3885a03faef42.png)

Now, we determine the value of $Φ(2.01)$ from the table:

- We first select the row that corresponds to $2.0$ and the column that corresponds to $0.01.$

- Then, we take the value that lies at the intersection:

| $z$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,2.0\,$ | $\,0.9778\,$ | $\,0.9783\,$ | $\,0.9788\,$ |
| $\,2.1\,$ | $\,0.9826\,$ | $\,0.9830\,$ | $\,0.9834\,$ |
| $\,2.2\,$ | $\,0.9864\,$ | $\,0.9868\,$ | $\,0.9871\,$ |

Therefore, according to the table, we have

$$
P(Z\le 2.01)=Φ(2.01)=0.9778.
$$
